tests.notes: storage -> memory assignment copies; mutating the memory copy does not write back to storage
memory -> storage state variable assignment copies elements and resizes the storage array; later memory writes do not affect storage
a calldata array can be assigned directly to a storage state variable (copy)
memory -> memory assignment and passing to an internal memory parameter alias the same region rather than copying
assigning one storage state array to another copies; contrast with a local storage pointer, which aliases
storage struct -> memory struct copies all fields; mutating the copy leaves storage unchanged
memory struct -> storage struct and memory struct -> storage array push both copy
returning a storage array from a public function performs an implicit storage -> memory copy at the return statement
memory -> calldata is legal across an external call (this.f(m)) because the argument is ABI-encoded; contrast with 012
a memory array cannot be bound to a local storage pointer; a storage pointer must refer to data that lives in storage
a calldata array cannot be bound to a local storage pointer; copying calldata into a storage state variable (003) is a copy, not a pointer binding
memory array cannot be passed to an internal function with a calldata parameter; no implicit memory -> calldata conversion without an external call
storage array cannot be passed to an internal function with a calldata parameter; same root cause as 012
